findings.title: track_visit! stores the topic id as user_id when given a plain user id
findings.body: In `track_visit!(topic, user)`, the fallback is `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic`, which uses `topic` where `user` is meant. The caller in TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic passes an integer (`TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id`), so `user_id` silently becomes the topic id. The visit timestamp is then written to whichever TopicUser row has user_id equal to the topic id (another user's row), or a bogus TopicUser row is inserted for that wrong user. The real visitor's last_visited_at is never updated. This is pre-existing, but the method is touched by this PR and the bug directly affects the visit tracking the feature relies on.

findings.title: Unsubscribe writes notification_level directly, so the mute is reverted on the next read
findings.body: `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which normally sets `notifications_reason_id` to `user_changed` and `notifications_changed_at`, and publishes the MessageBus `notification_level_change`. Because the reason stays nil, `TopicUser.update_last_read` (its CASE clause checks `tu.notifications_reason_id is null` and total_msecs_viewed over the auto-track threshold) will set notification_level back to tracking the next time the user reads the topic. The unsubscribe is therefore undone silently for most rows. Using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` would avoid this and keep open browser sessions in sync.

findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` can return nil, for example when a logged-in user opens the unsubscribe URL for a public topic they can see but never read or were never notified about. The next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, producing a 500 instead of a sensible response. Nil should be handled, for example by creating the record through `TopicUser.change` or by redirecting.

findings.title: Unsubscribe changes state on a GET request
findings.body: The action mutates the user's notification level but is routed as GET (routes.rb `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). Email link scanners and link-preview prefetchers that follow URLs in mail will silently mute topics for recipients. Because Rails forgery protection does not cover GET, any page that can embed the URL can also mute topics for a logged-in user. A POST (or a confirmation step) is the usual safeguard for state-changing unsubscribe links.

findings.title: Unsubscribe lowers watching/tracking topics only to regular, contradicting the message shown
findings.body: For a topic at tracking or watching, the code sets notification_level to regular rather than muted. Regular still notifies on replies and mentions, yet the page (client.en.yml `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`) says "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>". For a watching topic the user keeps receiving reply and mention notifications after clicking. The toggle-like branching (regular goes to muted, anything above goes to regular) is also undocumented and hard to reason about. Either the behaviour should always mute, or the message should describe the actual new level.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires an unsubscribe_url interpolation argument
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` string now contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will make `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` in MessageBuilder#body and #html_part raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument, which fails sending the email. The only in-repo caller (send_notification_email) now passes the value, but plugins or other code paths using the existing `add_unsubscribe_link` option break. The option needs a default, or the template should be guarded.

findings.title: New unsubscribe endpoint has no specs
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe adds login enforcement, slug redirects, notification-level toggling, a persistence call and a new render path, but no controller or request spec covers any of it. The notification-level branching, the 301 redirect for mismatched slugs, the behaviour for a missing TopicUser, and the persisted state after the call are all untested. Given the bugs above, a spec would have caught at least the nil-record and reverted-mute problems.

findings.title: Spec passes unsubscribe_url but never checks that the topic unsubscribe link is rendered
findings.body: The `add_unsubscribe_link: true` context now passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`, but the only body assertion checks for the user preferences URL. Nothing verifies that the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the body or html_part, so a regression that drops `%{unsubscribe_url}` from the template or the interpolation would go unnoticed.
